title: Proton pump inhibitors and vascular function: a prospective cross-over pilot study
authors: Ghebremariam YT, Cooke JP, Khan F, Thakker RN, Chang P, Shah NH, et al.
followUp: two 4-week treatment periods separated by a 2-week washout
population: Adults aged 18 or older, 11 healthy and 10 with established cardiovascular disease; open-label crossover of lansoprazole 30 mg or placebo once daily
funder: This pilot study was funded by grants from the Translational Research and Applied Medicine (TRAM) Program in the Department of Medicine at Stanford University; also supported in part by NIH grants (1R01 EY02060901, 1U01 HL100397) and internal funding from the Houston Methodist Research Institute; YTG by Stanford, the Tobacco-Related Disease Research Program, NHLBI (1K01 HL118683-01) and HMRI.
authorConflicts: YTG and JPC are inventors on Stanford patents protecting agents that modulate the NOS/DDAH pathway and co-founders of Altitude Pharma Inc, a biotech developing products that regulate the NOS/DDAH pathway.
result: Plasma ADMA rose more on lansoprazole than on placebo, more so in participants with vascular disease, but the differences were not statistically significant; PPI use did not impair flow-mediated vasodilation (EndoPAT). The authors call for larger, long-term blinded trials.
